s0101.literal: From Xia and Yin down, this statute has not been changed.
s0101.idiomatic: Since Xia and Yin, this institution has never been altered.

s0102.literal: We humbly note: Empress Zhaocheng had the virtue of Tai Si and already shares sacrifice in Ruizong's chamber;
s0102.idiomatic: It is submitted that Empress Zhaocheng possessed Tai Si's virtue and already shares sacrifice with Ruizong;

s0103.literal: then Empress Suming lacked the standing of Qi's mother and ought on her own to have a separate temple established.
s0103.idiomatic: whereas Empress Suming did not have Qi's mother's rank and should have a temple of her own.

s0104.literal: We respectfully cite the Zhou Rites: "Play Yi ze, sing Xiao lü, to offer to the former consort"—that is Jiang Yuan.
s0104.idiomatic: The Zhou Rites state that playing Yi ze and singing Xiao lü to honor a former consort refers to Jiang Yuan.

s0105.literal: Jiang Yuan was consort of Emperor Ku and mother of Hou Ji; a temple was specially established for her, named Bi Palace.
s0105.idiomatic: Jiang Yuan was Emperor Ku's consort and Hou Ji's mother; she was given a separate temple called Bi Palace.

s0106.literal: Also the Ritual Disquisitions says Fu Xi's discussion of Jin states: "Empress Xuande of Jin Emperor Jianwen, since she was not allotted shared sacrifice, built a palace outside; at the seasons one went to the temple to offer sacrifice only.
s0106.idiomatic: The Ritual Disquisitions also cites Fu Xi on Jin: when Empress Xuande of Emperor Jianwen was denied shared sacrifice, a palace was built outside and seasonal offerings were made there alone.

s0107.literal: " Now Empress Suming has no position for complementary enshrinement; we ask, following Jiang Yuan and Empress Xuande, to have a separate temple and placement, the four seasons' sacrifices as the old observances."
s0107.idiomatic: Empress Suming likewise has no place for enshrinement; we ask that she, like Jiang Yuan and Empress Xuande, have a separate temple with seasonal sacrifices as before."

s0109.literal: Thereupon the tablet of Empress Zhaocheng was moved to share sacrifice in Ruizong's chamber; only the tablet of Suming was left in Yikun Temple.
s0109.idiomatic: The tablet of Empress Zhaocheng was then moved to Ruizong's chamber, leaving only Suming's tablet in Yikun Temple.

s0110.literal: At that time Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao again, with ritual officials, submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that revering the clan and honoring ancestors, enjoying virtue and exalting grace, must rectify names to illuminate the statutes of the age—this is ritual.
s0110.idiomatic: Director Jiang Jiao and the ritual officials again memorialized: "We hear that revering ancestors and exalting grace require correct titles to honor the age's laws—that is ritual.

s0111.literal: We note in the Grand Temple Empress Zetian is enshrined with Emperor Gaozong Tianhuang Dadi, the inscription reading "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."
s0111.idiomatic: In the Grand Temple Empress Zetian shares sacrifice with Emperor Gaozong, inscribed as "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."

s0112.literal: We trace how in the past she held favored rank and personally received the entrustment; she then assumed great government, the affair being one of expedient power.
s0112.idiomatic: She once held favored rank, received the late emperor's trust, and took power as an expedient measure.

s0113.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong the imperial title was already removed.
s0113.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong her imperial title had already been removed.

s0114.literal: Cen Xi and others were unversed in the body of government and again inscribed an imperial name.
s0114.idiomatic: Cen Xi and others, ignorant of governance, restored an imperial title on the inscription.

s0115.literal: If the imperial title is again made to endure long, I fear it is not the general statute of the sagely court.
s0115.idiomatic: To let an imperial title stand again would violate court precedent.

s0116.literal: The seven temples are the temples of the High Ancestor, the Divine Yao Emperor.
s0116.idiomatic: The seven temples are those of the High Ancestor, Emperor Shen Yao.

s0117.literal: Father zhao, son mu; ancestral virtue and clan achievement—none but sons of emperors and grandsons of Heaven, those who mount Qian and issue from Zhen, may ascend to enshrinement there.
s0117.idiomatic: Father-zhao, son-mu, ancestral merit—only imperial sons and heaven's grandsons who received the mandate may be enshrined there.

s0118.literal: But the empress enshrined in the temple, sharing sacrifice with Gaozong, by old title and statute ought not be called emperor.
s0118.idiomatic: Yet as consort sharing Gaozong's sacrifices, her old titles should not include "emperor."

s0119.literal: Now the imperial tomb day draws near and ascent to enshrinement is not distant; we ask to declare the announcement rite and remove the words "Holy Emperor," inscribing simply "Empress Zetian Wu."
s0119.idiomatic: With her enshrinement near, we ask to perform the announcement rite, drop "Holy Emperor," and inscribe only "Empress Zetian Wu."

s0121.literal: At that time a separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the king establishes the body—this is called the model;
s0121.idiomatic: A separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou wrote: "A king's institutions are his model;

s0122.literal: the rise of the model in fact relies on taking antiquity as teacher;
s0122.idiomatic: and models must learn from antiquity;

s0123.literal: the Way of taking antiquity as teacher must rectify names;

s0124.literal: names and reality solidly ought to match each other.

s0125.literal: As for the ancestral temple, the greatest of rites—how can it be lost!
s0125.idiomatic: In the ancestral temple, the greatest rite—how can it be neglected!

s0126.literal: Ritual: the ancestor has merit, the clan lord has virtue.
s0126.idiomatic: Ritual holds that ancestors have merit and clan lords have virtue.

s0127.literal: The temples of ancestor and clan lord are not destroyed for a hundred generations.
s0127.idiomatic: Ancestor and clan-lord temples stand for a hundred generations.

s0128.literal: Thus Yin's Tai Jia was called Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, Wu Ding Gaozong.
s0128.idiomatic: Yin's Tai Jia was styled Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, and Wu Ding Gaozong.

s0129.literal: Zhou honored King Wen and King Wu.
s0129.idiomatic: Zhou honored Kings Wen and Wu.

s0130.literal: Han made Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.
s0130.idiomatic: Han styled Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.

s0131.literal: Afterward generations had those styled "zong," all because they regulated the realm within the four seas and their virtue and grace could be honored; ranked in zhao and mu, they were expected not to be destroyed.
s0131.idiomatic: Later rulers styled "zong" when their virtue filled the realm and merited lasting place in the zhao-mu sequence.

s0132.literal: The meaning of ancestor and clan lord—is it not great!
s0132.idiomatic: The weight of "ancestor" and "zong" is immense.

s0133.literal: Moreover Emperor Xiaojing's position stopped at the Eastern Palace; he never faced south. His sagely Way indeed topped the heir, yet his moral teaching did not spread through the realm—establishing a temple and styling him zong, I fear, is not fitting the body of ritual.
s0133.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing never ruled; though his virtue surpassed other heirs, his teaching did not reach the realm—calling him "zong" does not fit ritual.

s0134.literal: Moreover a separate sleeping temple was raised, not entering zhao and mu; searching the sacrifice canon, what meaning is there in calling him zong?
s0134.idiomatic: A separate shrine outside the zhao-mu line cannot be called "zong" under the sacrifice canon.

s0135.literal: Yet the temple name Yizong would be spoken for ten thousand generations.
s0135.idiomatic: Yet the temple name Yizong would stand for ages.

s0136.literal: By your servant's shallow knowledge, I privately deem it impossible.
s0136.idiomatic: In my humble view it should not be done.

s0137.literal: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual.
s0137.idiomatic: Please have the offices review this and align it with ritual.

s0138.literal: Thereupon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices asked to use his posthumous title "Xiaojing" as the temple designation.
s0138.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices then proposed his posthumous title Xiaojing as the temple name.

s0140.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Xuanzong was about to travel to the eastern capital, but the Grand Temple buildings collapsed; he therefore moved the seven temples' tablets to Taiji Hall.
s0140.idiomatic: In the fifth year's first month Xuanzong planned to visit the eastern capital; when the Grand Temple collapsed, he moved all seven tablets to Taiji Hall.

s0141.literal: Xuanzong wore plain dress and avoided the main hall, halted court for three days, personally visited the tablets in Taiji Hall, and afterward set out for the eastern capital.
s0141.idiomatic: He wore mourning dress, avoided the main hall, suspended court for three days, visited the tablets in Taiji Hall, then traveled east.

s0142.literal: He then ordered the relevant offices to repair the Grand Temple.
s0142.idiomatic: He ordered repairs to the Grand Temple.

s0143.literal: The next year the temple was completed; Xuanzong returned to the capital and performed the rite of personal complementary enshrinement.
s0143.idiomatic: When the temple was finished the next year, he returned and performed the enshrinement rite in person.

s0144.literal: When the relevant offices drafted observances, on the day of complementary sacrifice the imperial carriage was to set out from within the palace. Xuanzong said to Song Jing and Su Ting: "Rites require fasting first, to align the mind. Per the observances, on the day of sacrifice the carriage sets out from Daming Palace, and the rite is performed at dawn; even if one sets out before the stars fade, one still arrives only after the hour has shifted—how can a dawn rite be kept? Moreover I dare not lodge in the fasting palace yet rest in the main hall. A fasting palace should be set up at the temple; on the fifth day go to the traveling palace to keep fast, on the sixth perform the rite at dawn—then it may accord with ritual." Jing and the rest praised the sagely feeling as profound and utmost, and asked to carry it out at once.
s0144.idiomatic: The offices drafted rites requiring the emperor to leave the palace on the enshrinement day. Xuanzong told Song Jing and Su Ting: "Rites require fasting first, to align the mind. Per the observances, on the day of sacrifice the carriage sets out from Daming Palace, and the rite is performed at dawn; even if one sets out before the stars fade, one still arrives only after the hour has shifted—how can a dawn rite be kept? Moreover I dare not lodge in the fasting palace yet rest in the main hall. A fasting palace should be set up at the temple; on the fifth day go to the traveling palace to keep fast, on the sixth perform the rite at dawn—then it may accord with ritual." They praised his devotion and asked to follow the revised plan immediately.

s0145.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to revise the observances.
s0145.idiomatic: An edict ordered the rites revised.

s0146.literal: On the sixth day Xuanzong on foot went from the fasting palace to the Grand Temple, entered by the east gate, and took his standing position.
s0146.idiomatic: On the sixth day he walked from the fasting palace to the Grand Temple, entered the east gate, and took his place.

s0147.literal: Music played the Nine Completes; he ascended the eastern steps and performed the libation and offering rite.
s0147.idiomatic: The Nine Completes were played; he ascended the east steps and offered libation.

s0148.literal: Reaching Ruizong's chamber, he bowed prostrate and sobbed; attendants all wept.
s0148.idiomatic: At Ruizong's chamber he prostrated himself and wept, and his attendants wept with him.

s0149.literal: A man of Henan prefecture, Sun Pingzi, came to the gate and stated: "Emperor Xiaojing of Zhongzong, having succeeded the great succession, ought not be moved to a separate temple."
s0149.idiomatic: Sun Pingzi of Henan memorialized: "Emperor Xiaojing of Zhongzong succeeded the throne and should not be kept in a separate temple."

s0150.literal: Xuanzong ordered the chancellor to summon Pingzi and the ritual officials to settle whether it was permissible; Court of Imperial Sacrifices Academician Su Xian and others stubbornly held to the prior discussion.
s0150.idiomatic: Xuanzong had the chancellor convene Pingzi and the ritualists; Su Xian and others clung to the earlier decision.

s0151.literal: Pingzi was sharp in debate; what he cited all had canonical basis—Xian and the rest could not bend him.
s0151.idiomatic: Pingzi argued forcefully with scriptural citations the ritualists could not refute.

s0152.literal: At that time Su Ting held government affairs; because Xian was his elder cousin's brother, he quite factionally aided him, and Pingzi's discussion in the end could not be carried out.
s0152.idiomatic: Su Ting, then in power, favored his cousin Su Xian, and Pingzi's proposal was rejected.

s0153.literal: Pingzi's discussion did not cease; he was then demoted to metropolitan magistrate of Kang prefecture, still sent under escort to his post, not permitted east or west.
s0153.idiomatic: When Pingzi persisted, he was exiled as magistrate of Kang and escorted to his post under guard.

s0154.literal: Pingzi on taking up his post soon died.

s0155.literal: Though Pingzi was demoted at the time, discussants deeply took his words as correct.
s0155.idiomatic: Despite his punishment, most officials thought him right.

s0156.literal: In the first month of the tenth year an edict stated: "I have heard that kings take the times to establish teaching and shape ritual according to affairs; modification and preservation take fitness as root, selection and rejection take timeliness as foremost. Thus the way of increase and decrease has distinctions, and the use of substance and ornament differs. Moreover utmost virtue is called filial piety, whereby one reaches the spirits; the great affair is sacrifice, whereby one reverence the ancestral temple. The state holds the calendar and mandate, repeated glory and heaped splendor; the four quarters take their succession from its illumination, and seven generations can display its virtue. I inherit and guard the great enterprise, reverently uphold the sagely design, always mindful of bright service, never failing in sacrifice. I have reviewed the classics and inquired into old institutions: far off, Xia and Yin differed in affairs; near at hand, Han and Jin differed in the Way. Though ritual texts are not one, solemn reverence is not two. I hold that to establish love beginning with kin teaches people harmony; to establish respect beginning with elders teaches people order. Thus I lead by ritual and follow feeling; sometimes teaching is preserved in the Way, sometimes ritual follows the times. I will create institutions according to fitness—how can I be bound by antiquity and limited to today? Moreover as affection diminishes with descent in mourning grades, temples are abolished with removal and destruction. Though one looks to ancient instruction and ritual is not violated, yet when I speak forever of filial thought, feeling is not yet satisfied. Seasonal offerings then stop—how can love and honor be complete in ritual? Having prayers yet sacrificing is not virtue overflowing in lasting transmission. The removed chambers should be ranked as main chambers, so kin is not exhausted yet distant is not abolished; the temple preserves the appearance, the ancestor is still honored in establishment. Thus the four seasons may be offered without gap for destroyed tablets; for a hundred generations without removal, not only at the founding temple. This is called changing to fit ritual, acting to hit the center; the solemn matching rite can be exalted, the dignified harmony is here. Moreover brother succeeding brother has clear text in antiquity. Now Zhongzong's tablet still dwells in a separate place; searching the old facts, the court is not at ease—move it to the main temple to display the great canon. Still create nine chambers; order the relevant offices to choose a day, announce, and move."
s0156.idiomatic: In the tenth year's first month the emperor issued an edict: "I have heard that kings take the times to establish teaching and shape ritual according to affairs; modification and preservation take fitness as root, selection and rejection take timeliness as foremost. Thus the way of increase and decrease has distinctions, and the use of substance and ornament differs. Moreover utmost virtue is called filial piety, whereby one reaches the spirits; the great affair is sacrifice, whereby one reverence the ancestral temple. The state holds the calendar and mandate, repeated glory and heaped splendor; the four quarters take their succession from its illumination, and seven generations can display its virtue. I inherit and guard the great enterprise, reverently uphold the sagely design, always mindful of bright service, never failing in sacrifice. I have reviewed the classics and inquired into old institutions: far off, Xia and Yin differed in affairs; near at hand, Han and Jin differed in the Way. Though ritual texts are not one, solemn reverence is not two. I hold that to establish love beginning with kin teaches people harmony; to establish respect beginning with elders teaches people order. Thus I lead by ritual and follow feeling; sometimes teaching is preserved in the Way, sometimes ritual follows the times. I will create institutions according to fitness—how can I be bound by antiquity and limited to today? Moreover as affection diminishes with descent in mourning grades, temples are abolished with removal and destruction. Though one looks to ancient instruction and ritual is not violated, yet when I speak forever of filial thought, feeling is not yet satisfied. Seasonal offerings then stop—how can love and honor be complete in ritual? Having prayers yet sacrificing is not virtue overflowing in lasting transmission. The removed chambers should be ranked as main chambers, so kin is not exhausted yet distant is not abolished; the temple preserves the appearance, the ancestor is still honored in establishment. Thus the four seasons may be offered without gap for destroyed tablets; for a hundred generations without removal, not only at the founding temple. This is called changing to fit ritual, acting to hit the center; the solemn matching rite can be exalted, the dignified harmony is here. Moreover brother succeeding brother has clear text in antiquity. Now Zhongzong's tablet still dwells in a separate place; searching the old facts, the court is not at ease—move it to the main temple to display the great canon. Still create nine chambers; order the relevant offices to choose a day, announce, and move."

s0157.literal: In spring of the eleventh year Xuanzong returned to the capital and issued an edict: "To exalt and build the ancestral temple is the greatest of rites; to pursue filial sacrifice is the utmost of virtue. Now the ancestor is established to honor, kin have no removal order; ever mindful of solemn matching, utmost purity is applied; rafters and beams are exalted, libation and offering are then bestowed. Looking on this slight virtue, I have received the suburban sacrifice—not personally, not in person—how can I display sincere reverence? The nineteenth day of the eighth month should be used to reverently behold the nine chambers." Thereupon Xuandi was posthumously honored as Xianzu and again ranked in the main chamber; Guangdi as Yizu; and Zhongzong's tablet was also returned to the Grand Temple.
s0157.idiomatic: That spring Xuanzong returned and decreed: "To exalt and build the ancestral temple is the greatest of rites; to pursue filial sacrifice is the utmost of virtue. Now the ancestor is established to honor, kin have no removal order; ever mindful of solemn matching, utmost purity is applied; rafters and beams are exalted, libation and offering are then bestowed. Looking on this slight virtue, I have received the suburban sacrifice—not personally, not in person—how can I display sincere reverence? The nineteenth day of the eighth month should be used to reverently behold the nine chambers." Xuandi was then honored as Xianzu in the main hall, Guangdi as Yizu, and Zhongzong's tablet was restored to the Grand Temple.

s0158.literal: When he was about to perform personal complementary enshrinement, rain stopped it.
s0158.idiomatic: Rain halted the planned personal enshrinement.

s0159.literal: He then ordered the relevant offices to perform the affair.
s0159.idiomatic: He had the offices carry out the rite instead.

s0160.literal: The old Zhongzong temple in the capital was then torn down.
s0160.idiomatic: Zhongzong's former capital temple was demolished.

s0161.literal: In the eastern capital's old temple, the tablet of Xiaojing was first moved to complementary enshrinement there.
s0161.idiomatic: Xiaojing's tablet was first enshrined in the eastern capital's old temple.

s0162.literal: The old Xiaojing temple in Congshan Lane was also ordered demolished.
s0162.idiomatic: The Xiaojing shrine in Congshan Lane was also torn down.

s0163.literal: In the twenty-first year Xuanzong again specially ordered the tablet of Empress Suming moved to share sacrifice in Ruizong's chamber; the old Yikun Temple was still made the Suming Abbey.
s0163.idiomatic: In year twenty-one he moved Suming's tablet to Ruizong's chamber and converted Yikun Temple into Suming Abbey.

s0164.literal: In the tenth month, as Emperor Daizong's tablet was about to be enshrined, Director of Ritual Yan Zhenqing, because the Yuan Emperor's generations were already distant, per ritual ought to be removed, and asked to move him to the western side chamber.
s0164.idiomatic: When Daizong's tablet was to be installed, Yan Zhenqing argued that the Yuan Emperor was too remote by generation and should be moved to the western side chamber.

s0166.literal: , when Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined, Xianzu and Yizu had already undergone successive removal.
s0166.idiomatic: When Xuanzong and Suzong were enshrined, Xianzu and Yizu had already been removed in turn.

s0167.literal: We note Emperor Daizong the Filial, at the end of wailing and enshrinement, ought to move up one chamber.
s0167.idiomatic: Daizong's enshrinement after mourning requires shifting one chamber upward.

s0168.literal: The Yuan Emperor's generations are already distant; his tablet per ritual should be removed; at the di and cha rites he would then be offered sacrifice.
s0168.idiomatic: The Yuan Emperor is too remote; his tablet should be removed and honored only at the great di and cha sacrifices.

s0169.literal: Thereupon the Yuan Emperor was removed to the western side chamber and Daizong's tablet was enshrined.
s0169.idiomatic: The Yuan Emperor was moved to the western side chamber and Daizong was enshrined.

s0170.literal: In the eleventh month, as Emperor Dezong's tablet was about to be enshrined, Director of Ritual Du Huangchang and ritual officials Wang Jing and others asked to move Gaozong's tablet to the western side chamber.
s0170.idiomatic: When Dezong's tablet was to be installed, Du Huangchang and Wang Jing proposed moving Gaozong to the western side chamber.

s0171.literal: Their discussion stated: "From Han and Wei down, institutions differ.
s0171.idiomatic: They argued: "Since Han and Wei, practice has varied.

s0172.literal: In antiquity the ancestor had merit and the clan lord had virtue—both are names not destroyed.
s0172.idiomatic: Antiquity held that meritorious ancestors and virtuous clan lords were never removed.

s0173.literal: From Eastern Han, Wei, and Jin through Chen and Sui, they gradually departed from the classic intent; descendants took extolling beauty as foremost; from Guangwu down all had ancestor-and-clan-lord designations.
s0173.idiomatic: From Eastern Han through Sui, courts increasingly praised forebears for flattery; after Guangwu nearly every emperor received "ancestor" or "zong" titles.

s0174.literal: Thus when successive removal exhausted kin, ritual also shifted in turn; the state's nine temples' honor all follow Zhou's system.
s0174.idiomatic: As kinship lapsed, tablets were removed in turn; the nine-temple system follows Zhou.

s0175.literal: We note the Great Ancestor Emperor Jing received the mandate from Heaven, first enfeoffed the primal root—his virtue equals Zhou's Hou Ji.
s0175.idiomatic: Great Ancestor Jing received Heaven's mandate and founded the line, like Zhou's Hou Ji.

s0176.literal: The High Ancestor Emperor Shen Yao was the dynasty's first reign, the myriad leaves' inheritance—his virtue equals Zhou's King Wen.
s0176.idiomatic: High Ancestor Shen Yao began the dynasty, like Zhou's King Wen.

s0177.literal: Emperor Taizong the Cultural responded to Heaven, quelled disorder, and handed down the succession—his virtue equals Zhou's King Wu.
s0177.idiomatic: Taizong pacified the realm and established the succession, like Zhou's King Wu.

s0178.literal: Zhou in the suburbs honored Hou Ji and in the temple took King Wen as ancestor and King Wu as clan lord; sagely Tang in the suburbs honors Emperor Jing and in the temple takes the High Ancestor as ancestor and Taizong as clan lord—all in the canon of non-removal.
s0178.idiomatic: Zhou sacrificed to Hou Ji and honored Wen and Wu in the temple; Tang sacrifices to Jing, with Shen Yao as ancestor and Taizong as zong—all never removed.

s0179.literal: Emperor Gaozong is now outside the three zhao and three mu—called kin exhausted; with a new tablet entering the temple, ritual requires successive removal, stored in the first side chamber from the west; each di and cha month he is jointly offered as usual.
s0179.idiomatic: Gaozong now stands outside the zhao-mu line; when Dezong enters, Gaozong should move to the westernmost side chamber and still share in di and cha offerings.

s0180.literal: Thereupon Gaozong's tablet was removed to the western side chamber and Dezong's tablet was enshrined.
s0180.idiomatic: Gaozong was moved to the western side chamber and Dezong was enshrined.

s0181.literal: In the seventh month, as Emperor Shunzong's tablet was about to be enshrined, the relevant offices were doubtful about removal and destruction; Court of Imperial Sacrifices Academician Wang Jing submitted a proposal, saying:
s0181.idiomatic: When Shunzong's tablet was to be installed, the offices debated removal; Academician Wang Jing proposed:

s0182.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of that month Director of Ritual Du Huangchang memorialized: "Emperor Shunzong's tablet has already ascended to complementary enshrinement in the Grand Temple; after announcing removal, it should shift in turn.
s0182.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth Du Huangchang reported: "Shunzong is already in the Grand Temple; after the removal announcement his predecessors should shift.

s0183.literal: Emperor Zhongzong's tablet is now outside the three zhao and three mu; per ritual he should be moved to the Grand Temple's first side chamber from the west; on each di and cha day he is jointly offered as usual."
s0183.idiomatic: Zhongzong's tablet is outside the zhao-mu line and should move to the first western side chamber, sharing di and cha offerings as before."

s0184.literal: Thereupon Zhongzong's tablet was removed to the western side chamber and Shunzong's tablet was enshrined.
s0184.idiomatic: Zhongzong was moved to the western side chamber and Shunzong was enshrined.

s0185.literal: The relevant offices had earlier, because the imperial tomb was nearing completion, discussed the rite of temple removal.
s0185.idiomatic: Earlier, as the imperial tomb neared completion, the offices had debated temple removal.

s0186.literal: The relevant offices took Zhongzong as a restoration ruler and entitled to the position not removed for a hundred generations.
s0186.idiomatic: They argued Zhongzong was a restoration emperor who should never be removed.

s0187.literal: The chancellor summoned historiographer Jiang Wu to question him; Wu replied: "Zhongzong succeeded at Gaozong's coffin; by then his years were already mature.
s0187.idiomatic: The chancellor asked historiographer Jiang Wu, who replied: "Zhongzong took the throne at Gaozong's death when already mature.

s0188.literal: When the empress dowager usurped, the sacred vessel shifted in secret.
s0188.idiomatic: When the empress dowager seized power, the throne was lost.

s0189.literal: Afterward, relying on Zhang Jianzhi and others in common plot, the imperial fortune was twice restored.
s0189.idiomatic: Later Zhang Jianzhi and his allies restored him—twice.

s0190.literal: This is roughly like a return to correctness; I fear he may not be styled a restoration ruler.
s0190.idiomatic: That resembles mere restoration, not the "restoration emperor" of ritual theory.

s0191.literal: What is not lost by oneself but restored by oneself is called restoration—Han Guangwu and Jin Yuandi are cases.
s0191.idiomatic: True restoration means regaining what one lost oneself, as with Guangwu or Jin's Yuandi.

s0192.literal: What is lost by oneself but restored through others—Jin's Emperor Hui and Emperor An are cases.
s0192.idiomatic: Losing the throne and recovering it through others, as with Jin's Hui and An, is different.

s0193.literal: Now Zhongzong's affair is the same as the two emperors Hui and An; he cannot be a ruler not removed.
s0193.idiomatic: Zhongzong matches Hui and An and cannot be a permanently enshrined ruler.

s0194.literal: The relevant offices also said: "The Five Kings had the achievement of twice settling the altars of soil and grain; if Zhongzong's temple is now moved, the Five Kings will forever cut off the precedent of shared sacrifice."
s0194.idiomatic: The offices added: "Moving Zhongzong would end the Five Kings' shared sacrifice forever."

s0195.literal: Wu said: Generally meritorious ministers sharing sacrifice only at di and cha years jointly eat in the Grand Temple; in ordinary times there is no offering rite.
s0195.idiomatic: Wu replied: Merit-sharing ministers are fed in the Grand Temple only at di and cha; otherwise they receive no regular offerings.

s0196.literal: Now moving Zhongzong's tablet—in di and cha years, destroyed-temple rulers are all arrayed in the Grand Temple; this is the same as the Five Kings' shared sacrifice, as before.
s0196.idiomatic: Moving Zhongzong still leaves the Five Kings honored at di and cha when removed rulers are assembled—no change for them.

s0197.literal: The relevant offices could not answer.

s0198.literal: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year, Vice Minister of Rites Li Jian memorialized the late emperor's posthumous title as Emperor Sheng Shen Zhang Wu Xiao and temple name Xianzong.
s0198.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifteenth year Li Jian proposed the posthumous title Sheng Shen Zhang Wu Xiao and temple name Xianzong for the late emperor.

s0199.literal: Earlier, Military Commissioner of Henan Li Yijian had submitted a discussion, saying: "Kings take as ancestor those with merit and as clan lord those with virtue.
s0199.idiomatic: Earlier Li Yijian of Henan had argued: "Kings honor meritorious ancestors and virtuous clan lords.

s0200.literal: The late emperor cut down rebels and bandits and repeatedly had military achievements; the temple name ought to be styled zu."
s0200.idiomatic: The late emperor suppressed rebellion with repeated military success; his temple name should be zu, not zong."
